text:
Allison Grant: Post-launch monitoring thread for profile pack defaults (Hosted canary). Dropping early adoption + spot-check notes here so we have one place.

Allison Grant: Current cohort status (as of this morning):
- Hosted: ~12% of traffic on profile pack defaults (flag `runtime.profile_pack.enabled=true` for canary cohort A)
- Dedicated: still opt-in only; 2 customer pools pinned via config override
- Private: none known yet (docs/helm changes merged but no installs reported)

Allison Grant: Dashboards:
- Runtime Profiles overview: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/runtime-profiles/overview
- Tail latency (p95/p99) by profile_id: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/runtime-profiles/tail-latency
- Kernel fallbacks: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/runtime-profiles/kernel-fallbacks
- Scheduler queue ms: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/runtime-profiles/scheduler-queue

Marcus Reed: Pulling numbers from the dashboard (last 6h, H100 pools only, chat+streaming endpoints):
- p50 TTFT: -2.8% vs pre-pack baseline
- p95 E2E: -1.6%
- p99 E2E: flat overall, but we have one workload bucket ("mixed short prefill + long decode") where p99 is +3-4% in us-east
- scheduler_queue_ms p99: +6ms in that bucket when concurrency spikes

Sofia Ivanova: That bucket is the one where queue prioritization is most sensitive. Can someone sanity-check the cohort is actually using the new workload bucket classifier? (I want to ensure we’re not mixing old scheduler defaults + new batching caps.)

Caleb Johnson: It is. Traces show `scheduling_mode=wb_v1` on the canary cohort. I can paste a sample trace id if helpful.

Omar El-Sayed: KV/memory signals (H100 canary vs control):
- kv_compaction_time_ms p95: +0.3ms (noise)
- kv_compaction_events/sec: slightly up (~8%) but not alarming
- fragmentation_estimate: stable
- OOM: none in H100 canary (0 events)

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel fallback rate is the one I’m watching. What’s the current `kernel_fallback_total / requests`?

Allison Grant: Over last 24h on H100:
- `kernel_choice=attn_v3`: ~94%
- `kernel_choice=attn_v2`: ~5.7%
- fallback counter (explicit) ~0.23% of requests
Mostly correlates with long-context prompts.

Yuki Sato: 0.23% fallback is within expectations, but can we confirm those fallbacks aren’t clustered on a specific driver version? We had that earlier mismatch on one pool.

Allison Grant: Good call. By driver label (limited cardinality, only major.minor):
- 535.154: 0.18%
- 535.161: 0.26%
- 550.54: 0.22%
No obvious outlier.

Sean Gallagher: SRE check: any SLO gates close to tripping? (p99 latency or 5xx)

Rafael Mendes: Canary gates are currently green. Error rates flat. The only thing that’s flirting with our “warn” threshold is p99 on that mixed bucket in us-east (not crossing the block threshold).

Mateo Alvarez: Re the +3-4% p99 on mixed bucket: can we confirm it’s not due to the batching default we previously reverted? (I want to make sure we’re not reintroducing the same behavior through profile selection.)

Lena Fischer: Looked at active knobs for the canary cohort via startup log summary. Batching is at the “safe” values after PR-24988. The difference is the per-profile queue limit + prefill/decode prioritization weights.

Noah Patel: +1. The runtime summary log shows:
- profile_id=h100_sxm_prod_v1
- scheduling_mode=wb_v1
- max_inflight_requests=??? (need to make sure this is consistently logged)
We might be missing one key knob in the log output for fast comparisons.

Connor O'Brien: Please file a follow-up to ensure the startup log + /debug include the full “top knobs” set (batching caps, queue limits, kv headroom, kernel variant). Otherwise release triage is painful.

Allison Grant: Ack. Minor follow-ups list (please add):
1) Add missing knob fields to startup summary + debug bundle (per INT-8831 ask)
2) Add breakdown panel for `scheduler_queue_ms` by workload_bucket *and* region (right now it’s hard to isolate)
3) Add driver version dimension to kernel fallback panel (we can keep it coarse)

Lauren Bishop: Customer spot-checks:
- SUP-21941 (Dedicated H100): customer reported p99 regression after runtime upgrade. We pinned profile_version back to known-good and p99 normalized. They’re asking how long until we ship a fix vs keep pinned.
- SUP-21958 (L40S): intermittent OOM under burst. Support workaround is “cap concurrency lower” + keep extra KV headroom.
Can runtime team confirm if the current L40S profile has the updated headroom defaults? (I don’t want support giving inconsistent guidance.)

Omar El-Sayed: L40S profile has the updated headroom as of PR-25071 (if they’re on runtime-1.22.x). If they’re on 1.21, they won’t have it.

Connor O'Brien: For SUP-21941: what exact runtime build are they on? If it’s the first 1.22 cut, we should recommend upgrading to the patch release (assuming we already merged the p99 fix).

Rafael Mendes: They’re on 1.22.0 (per ticket). Support pinned profile_version=1.0.0 and disabled “auto bump.” We should clarify if we want customers pinning to patch versions (1.0.1) or only major/minor.

Mateo Alvarez: Let’s not bikeshed in the ticket. For now: recommend pinning profile_version while we fix the mixed bucket queue weights + ship 1.0.1. Connor/Talia can align on the messaging.

Sahana Iyer: Perf-canary note: we’re currently gating on aggregate p95/p99 per SKU. We should add a gate for that mixed bucket specifically (since it’s where regressions hide). I’ll open a task if folks agree.

Sofia Ivanova: Agree. It’s exactly the bucket we tuned for. If we don’t gate it explicitly, we’ll keep rediscovering it in prod.

Hiro Tanaka: Also: long-context edge case that triggers attn_v3 -> v2 fallback is currently expected, but we should annotate that in expected behavior docs so SRE doesn’t page on it.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Alert thresholds: fallback alert should be “ticket” unless it correlates with latency deltas. We had some confusion yesterday.

Deploy Bot: runtime-prod-canary deploy complete (runtime-1.22.1-rc3) to cohort A. Kill-switch available: `runtime.profile_pack.enabled=false`.

Allison Grant: Action items I’m capturing:
- Sofia/Marcus: propose small adjustment to queue weights for mixed bucket (target: remove p99 +3-4% in us-east)
- Sahana: add perf-canary gate on mixed bucket p99 (warn->block if > +2% vs baseline)
- Allison/Caleb: improve dashboard slicing (bucket + region) + add coarse driver dimension to fallbacks
- Connor/Noah: expand startup log summary + ensure /health or /debug includes profile_id + profile_version + key knobs consistently
- Lauren/Omar: support guidance: L40S OOM mitigation = ensure runtime >= 1.22 w/ updated headroom + cap concurrency; document exact config keys to recommend

Mateo Alvarez: Thanks. Keep this thread alive for the next ~72h while the canary ramps. If we see p99 worsen or fallbacks spike, we flip the kill switch first and investigate second.
